thread:
jamie: Heads up — SignalBridge (acct: sb-4421) hit sustained 429 admission throttles on Dedicated pool `cedar` during their promo blast. They say TPS SLO violations (token/s), burst credits went to 0 and autoscaler didn't open extra nodes. Seeing user-facing latency spikes too. Can we triage? cc @mohammad @priya

priya: Got it. Can you paste the account id + a sample request id? Also running quick checks: admission controller logs, headroom metrics, burst credit ledger, autoscaler events. Is this isolated to cedar?

jamie: Account sb-4421, sample request id: r_20260317_az12_7f9. Repro: they replayed their campaign at ~11:02 UTC and saw immediate 429s. No auth errors (200 on auth). Only admission denies (429).

alex: Quick note — pool `cedar` max_nodes=4 and autoscaler policy is conservative (scale_delay=60s, ramp_factor=1). If node spinup hits quota it won't grow beyond 4. I saw scale attempts at 11:03 but nodes stayed at 4. Could be capacity/ASG cap or a preemptive headroom miscalc.

mohammad: Pulling admission metrics now. ops-bot, paste last hour admission_denials/time series.

ops-bot: admission_denials: [11:00:00: 12, 11:05:00: 48, 11:10:00: 112]  (total 172 in 30m)
ops-bot: avg_token_latency: 210ms
ops-bot: burst_credits(sb-4421)=0, last_refill=2026-03-14T03:02Z :warning:

billing-bot: account sb-4421 billing status: invoice_pending=true, auto_refill_disabled=true, committed_tier=dedicated-4gpu

priya: Interesting — burst credits are zero and auto_refill_disabled=true because of invoice_pending. That explains no refill but doesn't explain node scale failing. Two parallel issues: 1) admission controller refusing on zero burst credits; 2) autoscaler not increasing nodes due to pool hard cap or cloud quota.

jamie: Here's the user's repro curl (redacted keys):
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-sb-****" \
  -d '{"input":"short text","max_tokens":64}'
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "admission_denied", "reason": "burst_credits_exhausted", "pool":"cedar" }
```

priya: OK that response string is explicit. Root cause hypothesis: billing flow blocked auto-refill which left burst_credits at 0; admission controller denies strictly when credits=0; autoscaler couldn't scale because pool hit max_nodes or cloud account CPU/GPU quota. Fix path: short-term: refill credits & enable hosted fallback; medium: relax admission rule to allow small grace headroom when pending-invoice + alert billing; long-term: decouple auto-refill from invoice_pending for emergency SLOs.

alex: Immediate mitigation steps I recommend now:
1) Manually credit sb-4421 with 50k burst tokens (admin ledger call).
2) Temporarily increase cedar pool max_nodes to 6 and bump AWS ASG limit if needed.
3) Enable fallback routing for sb-4421 to hosted pool for 2 hours.
Commands:
```
# refill credits
ADMIN_TOKEN=redacted curl -X POST https://admin.internal/pools/ledger/refill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"account":"sb-4421","amount":50000}'

# adjust pool cap
ADMIN_TOKEN=redacted curl -X POST https://admin.internal/pools/cedar/resize \
  -d '{"max_nodes":6}'

# enable fallback
ADMIN_TOKEN=redacted curl -X POST https://admin.internal/accounts/sb-4421/fallback \
  -d '{"hosted_fallback":true,"ttl_minutes":120}'
```

mohammad: I'll run the commands. Starting refill now. Also can we add a quick admission-controller log patch to print credit checks so we can confirm behavior next spike?

ops-bot: refill job queued id=job_8902, status=running

billing-bot: note: because invoice_pending=true auto_refill_disabled flag is expected behavior. Manual refill allowed by ops. Recommend escalated billing contact to clear invoice or set emergency_refill policy.

jamie: After manual refill, customer tried a replay and saw errors drop from 429->200 but latency still slightly elevated. They confirm fail rate down to ~3%.

priya: Action plan captured:
- P0 (now): manual refill + pool cap bump + enable hosted fallback (mohammad + alex). Verify with replay.
- P1 (24h): patch admission controller to allow small grace tokens when invoice_pending but alert billing and product. Run canary for 48h.
- P2 (72h): autoscaler policy review — reduce scale_delay, add emergency burst nodes that ignore reserved commit up to a limit.
- P3 (post-mortem): billing UX change to allow emergency auto-refill for production SLOs and better alerting to customers.

alex: I'll open a PR for the autoscaler policy changes and a quick toggle for hosted-fallback per-account. Assign to priya for review.

mohammad: Refill completed. job_8902 -> success. Pool max_nodes bumped to 6. Fallback enabled for sb-4421. Monitoring now shows admission_denials falling.

ops-bot: admission_denials: [11:20:00: 8, 11:25:00: 2, 11:30:00: 0]  (total 10 in 20m) :white_check_mark:

jamie: Customer reported recovery and thanks the team. We'll follow up with billing to resolve invoice and close the loop.

priya: Filing incident ticket and scheduling post-mortem. I'll include load test (k6 script) to reproduce with mixed token size and ramp profile.

billing-bot: Noted — contacting SB billing contact now. invoice_pending -> cleared will re-enable auto_refill.

jamie: Great work. Marking thread resolved for now.
